About

I am an Applied Mathematics undergraduate interested in AI for Science and scientific machine learning. My research focuses on neural methods for multiphase flow simulation, alongside projects in computer vision, sports analytics, and AI-assisted education.

Publications & Manuscripts

Neural Curvature Estimation for Two-Phase Flow Simulations

First-author manuscript · In preparation

Neural interface-curvature estimation for multiphase flow, connecting learned local geometry with numerical simulation in Basilisk.

Project details

JAN 2026 — PRESENT SCIENTIFIC MACHINE LEARNING

Learning interface curvature from local level-set information, from synthetic training data to deployment in a multiphase flow solver.

  • Generated approximately 83.5 million samples across five grid resolutions.
  • Reduced MSE by factors of 5.6–260 versus second-order finite differences in matched-resolution tests.
  • Integrated standalone C inference into Basilisk’s CLSVOF solver; evaluated stationary bubble, capillary wave, and rising bubble cases.

Supervisor: Dr. Jiaqi Zhang

Python / PyTorch / C / Basilisk

Arrow Selection for Elite Series Arrows

Equal-contribution co-author · Submitted to Sports Engineering

High-speed motion analysis and physical measurements for data-driven selection of competition-grade arrows. Research at BNBU’s digital sports research center, 2025–2026.

Journal website ↗ · BNBU project overview ↗

Project details

Submission venue: Sports Engineering, published by Springer for the International Sports Engineering Association. Indexed in ESCI, EI Compendex, and Scopus. Journal Impact Factor: 1.4 (2025), as listed on the journal website. Manuscript submitted; not yet accepted.

JUL 2025 — MAY 2026 SCIENTIFIC COMPUTING

Research assistant on a joint project with the 18th Institute of CASC and Beijing Institute of Technology for the Chinese National Archery Team.

  • Conducted controlled shooting experiments and shaft-deflection measurements.
  • Developed high-speed-video analysis for launch velocity, launch angle, and trajectory deviation.
  • Linked physical measurements, shot kinematics, scores, and impact locations to support quantitative arrow selection.
Python / OpenCV / High-speed imaging

Projects

Automated Arrow-Impact Localization & Ring-Score Recognition

Computer Vision · June 2026–Present

A vision pipeline for detecting arrow impacts and recognizing ring scores under practical shooting conditions.

Project details

JUN 2026 — PRESENT COMPUTER VISION

Developing a vision pipeline for automated archery assessment, covering data curation, annotation, model training, and evaluation under practical shooting conditions.

  • Trained YOLO-based detection on public data and assessed generalization on self-collected target images.
  • The best preliminary preprocessing configuration achieved precision and recall above 70% on self-collected images.

Supervisors: Dr. Lidong Fang · Prof. Huaxiong Huang

Python / PyTorch / YOLO / OpenCV

AI-Assisted Education System

AI Engineering · September 2025–March 2026

A teaching-support system that turns course materials into editable lessons, assessments, and presentations through retrieval-augmented generation.

Project details

Developed during a remote research internship at Wanhoo Technology, supervised by Dr. Jiaqi Zhang.

  • Structured teaching materials with MinerU/OCR and integrated embedding, reranking, and chat models through SiliconFlow and Ollama.
  • Implemented editable assessments with five question types, three difficulty levels, natural-language revision, and DOCX export.
  • Integrated tool execution for multi-step tasks and deployed the system internally with Docker.

Python · RAG · MinerU/OCR · Docker
